newsitem.title: USA: Australia's Geoffrey Rush wins best actor Oscar.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Geoffrey Rush wins best actor Oscar.

text.p: Life inspired art for Australian actor Geoffrey Rush, who on Monday won the best acting Oscar for portraying the troubled concert pianist David Helfgott in the movie "Shine."
Earlier in the 3 1/2-hour Academy Awards ceremony, Helfgott himself brought the house down by playing "The Flight of the Bumblebee."
"You truly are an inspiration," said Rush in his acceptance speech, pointing out his countryman Helfgott in the star-studded audience for Hollywood's biggest night of the year.
The film, he said, was a tribute to Helfgott's attitude that "life is a circus" and the pianist made him believe in "working without a safety net."

The Oscar win, on his first nomination, completed a personal triumph for Rush, who earlier this year won the best actor Golden Globe from the Hollywood Foreign Press Association and also the Screen Actor's Guild award.
Helfgott, who is mentally troubled, is currently on a concert tour of the United States and his performances have been badly received by critics. However, the Oscar crowd gave him a standing ovation.
Asked later by reporters what he felt of the reaction to the real-life pianist he played on film, Rush said:
"Some of the critics' comments have been extremely unfair. But music critics hear things through sophisticated ears and David offers something different. He pours out his life on the keyboard."

The film tells how Helgott overcomes an overbearing father and mental problems with the help of his wife to become one of the world's most popular concert pianist. Armin Mueller-Stahl, who played his father in "Shine," missed out on a best supporting actor Oscar to Cuba Gooding Jr. from the movie "Jerry Maguire."
The film also also eclipsed as best picture by "The English Patient" with director Scott Hicks losing out to Anthony Minghella.
But Rush said his Academy Award was a tribute to everyone on the film.
"This is fantastic to get on behalf of our film," he said. "It represents a certain aspect of Australian film-making."
"I very fortunately got to meet David early in the process," he said, adding that Hicks had given him audio and video tapes of the pianist to study.
"David was not the sort of person to sit down and interview clinically," he said, adding that he had not met Helfgott yet after winning the Oscar.
"He will probably say something like 'brilliantissimo,' - he invents words."
Rush said that he had not expected to win. "I was pretty certain Billy Bob Thornton's name (for "Sling Blade") would come up (as winner) tonight. It was instinct. I must have shocking instincts."
Last year's best director winner, Mel Gibson, who was a roommate of Rush in 1979 when they co-starred in the play "Waiting for Godot" in Australia, bumped into Rush backstage Monday night.
"I knew you had it in you," Rush quoted Gibson as saying.
